answer: Because the karst calculation reruns each epoch, the reef weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the inlet settlement publishes the resulting shares. A tight ring of 80 clones therefore holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 37% independent neighbours on the funding graph. That is 14 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
